claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Arms delivered a record second quarter.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Revenue reached 1.44 billion, up 27% year over year, marking our fifth straight quarter of the fiscal year.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: License and other revenue grew 50% to 773 million, driven by our partners increasing their investment in the Arm Compute platform.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: This strong licensing momentum is an important leading indicator of future royalties, which we expect to accelerate as these new designs enter production.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Second quarter royalty revenue grew 8% to 670 million, with data center royalties doubling year over year.
claims.value: $670 million, up 8%; data center royalties doubled

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: And non-GAAP earnings per share increased 33% to 52 cents, while we continue to increase our investment in R&D.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: AI is driving unprecedented demand for compute across the cloud, devices, and autonomous systems, with Arm being the compute platform of choice.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: The IP business, where partners are increasing investment in the Arm Compute platform, deploying record numbers of Arm-based chips, and our new silicon business, where demand for the Arm AGI CPU is extremely strong.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Since launching the Arm AGU CPU in March, customer demand has continued to strengthen.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: We have secured purchase orders for multiple customers extending through calendar 2027, and first commercial deliveries remain on track for fiscal Q4-27.
claims.metric: Arm AGI CPU orders and deliveries

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Our confidence in achieving up to $2 billion of revenue in Arm AGI CPU across fiscal 2027 and 2028 has increased over the last 90 days.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Supported by additional supply and customer mix, we remain focused on expanding capacity to meet growing customer demand.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Our data center royalties doubled year over year, and Arm-based server market share at the top hyperscalers has more than tripled, from 15% in calendar 2024 to more than 50% in calendar 2025.
claims.metric: Data center royalties and hyperscaler server share

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: we now expect that share to exceed 60% by the end of calendar 2026.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Arm-based PCs have now reached 20% of global shipments.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Royalty revenue grew 50% year over year, driven by advanced driver assistance and in-vehicle infotainment.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: For the first time, our partners reported more than 10 billion Arm-based chips shipped in a single quarter.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Demand for Arm technology has never been stronger, as AI is driven more complex designs and greater demand for power efficient compute.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: That gives Arm two powerful growth engines, which we expect to accelerate revenue at a faster pace in the future.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: We delivered another strong quarter, with total revenue growing 27% year on year to $1.44 billion.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: This was a record for our second quarter and our second highest quarterly revenue ever, reflecting continued strength in our business.
claims.value: record Q2, second highest quarterly ever

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Licensed and other revenue was $773 million of 50% year on year, also a record for the second quarter and our second highest quarter ever.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: Licensed revenue was around $100 million higher than we had anticipated,

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: due to an acceleration of interest from customers wanting to sign long-term commitments to access Arm technology.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: During the quarter, we signed three new Arm total access agreements, bringing the total number of active ATA subscriptions to more than 60.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: This included one of our major customers signing their first ATA license.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: We also signed four additional compute subsystem licenses, two for data center chips and two for smartphones.

claims.speaker: Management
claims.quote: For established customers, these agreements broaden and deepen access to our future technology roadmap and provide an important foundation for Arm's future royalty growth.
